question: Should OpenClaw core adopt gateway-local multi-user Teams identity, exact-resource authorization, and the permanent `api.teams` plugin contract in this release direction?
rationale: Tests cannot decide whether OpenClaw should expand from its single-operator trust model into a supported multi-user identity and authorization platform or permanently commit the proposed plugin API and operational responsibilities.

options.title: Sponsor With Security Gates
options.body: Confirm the core direction, then require the canonical threat model, secops approval, real fresh-install and upgrade proof, and a clean rebase before merge.

options.title: Narrow To An Experiment
options.body: Keep the Teams portal and sharing flow experimental or plugin-owned until the smallest genuinely generic core authorization seam is proven.

options.title: Decline The Core Direction
options.body: Close this PR and the canonical issue if local multi-user identity and RBAC are not planned OpenClaw responsibilities.

recommendation.title: Sponsor With Security Gates
recommendation.body: Confirm the core direction, then require the canonical threat model, secops approval, real fresh-install and upgrade proof, and a clean rebase before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the Workspaces foundation and are the strongest available current-main product and gateway integration owner in the inspected history.
